newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev ends firmer at 212.80/213.30 per dlr.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev ends firmer at 212.80/213.30 per dlr.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed between 212.80-213.30 per dollar, up from 220-221 in the morning after a thin interbank trade in the afternoon as dollar supply persistently topped demand, dealers said.
"Low volumes traded in the afternoon as there were not many (dollar) sellers at 210-213 levs where the bids were," a commercial bank dealer said.

Foreign currency supply topped demand throughout the day and the central bank was seen buying dollars at 209-210 levs in the early afternoon in a bid to slow down the fast lev's rise against the dollar, dealers said.

A record high main rate of 25 percent monthly or 300 percent annually was the main reason for the rise of foreign currency supply this week as both banks and end customers switched into high yield lev-denominated investments, traders said.
"The lev gained some eight percent (against the dollar) this week," another dealer said.

The lev traded around 231 per dollar on Monday and about 236-237 just before the rate rise from previous 108 percent was announced by the central bank on September 23. @ -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
